title: Orszag–Tang vortex
description: A common starting point. Two ways to evolve the magnetic field. An independent reference to measure what each one gets right.

title: Supersonic turbulence decay
description: The first decay experiment: a Mach 10 random velocity field evolves freely, forming shocks and converting kinetic energy into heat.

columns.subtitle: Hydro baseline · MHD code with B = 0

cards.title: Watch the decay
cards.text: This is pure hydrodynamics through the original SIMD solver. Magnetic fields and the GLM variable remain zero.
cards.caption: 64³ · 121 saved frames · five initial box crossing times

cards.title: What changed
cards.text: Rejected trial states were retried at a smaller timestep; they are not part of the accepted solution.

cards.title: Validation
items: Mass and total-energy drift below 5 × 10⁻⁹
Finite, positive accepted states
B and ψ stayed exactly zero

cards.title: A hydro experiment
cards.text: CT evolves staggered magnetic fields. With B = 0, there is no magnetic constraint to compare in this run. No separate CT simulation was performed.

cards.title: Keep the comparison meaningful
cards.text: A future hydro comparison would test reconstruction, fluxes and time integration. It would not isolate GLM versus CT.

columns.subtitle: Initial conditions known · evolved reference absent

cards.title: What we know
cards.text: A periodic, solenoidal random field, seed 42. There is no exact analytical solution for the subsequent shocked flow.

cards.title: What is still missing
items: A finer, independently computed hydro reference
A matched initial-field resolution study
A check of sensitivity to numerical dissipation
cards.text: The current decay rate is a low-resolution demonstration, not a converged physical measurement.

cards.title: Equation of state matters
cards.text: γ = 1.01 is near-isothermal, not exactly isothermal. Dissipated kinetic energy heats the gas; the final rms sound speed is 1.224.

title: Prepared isothermal decay
description: Drive a periodic box toward Mach 10, switch the forcing off, then compare unchanged decay with a velocity-band perturbation. Preserved here as an earlier branch of the research.

columns.subtitle: Dedicated isothermal hydro solver · no GLM field

cards.title: Control and perturbed decay
cards.caption: Two hydrodynamic branches, not a GLM–CT comparison
cards.text: Four conserved fields: density and momentum. There is no magnetic field or total-energy equation.

cards.title: Both branches are hydrodynamic
cards.text: The control and gap branches use the same hydro solver. Neither is CT; the original GLM code is only the numerical-workflow lineage.

cards.title: Research status
cards.text: Spectral-gap work is parked while the active comparison focuses on GLM and CT in Orszag–Tang MHD. The saved experiment is retained for reproducibility.

columns.subtitle: Control branch and analytical checks · no exact flow

cards.title: The control is not exact truth
cards.text: It is the unperturbed branch of the same solver, useful for measuring response to the perturbation. It is not an independent numerical reference.

cards.title: A precisely defined perturbation
cards.text: The branches start with different kinetic energy. Subsequent differences cannot be attributed to the band location alone.

cards.title: Verified, and still open
items: Filtered velocity power is negligible initially
Momentum preserved within rounding
Kinetic-spectrum Parseval check passed
cards.text: Higher resolutions and multiple matched realizations would be needed for a physical recovery timescale. Band recovery does not directly measure spectral energy flux.

title: Small-amplitude acoustic wave
description: A smooth wave checks that the isothermal hydro solver transports sound accurately before we ask it to handle shocks and turbulence.

columns.subtitle: Hydro validation · not a GLM evolution test

cards.title: Watch the acoustic wave
cards.caption: 21 times · t = 0 → 0.2 · linked playback
cards.text: A new run with saved output times. The analytical wave is a linear approximation; the solver evolves nonlinear hydrodynamics.

cards.title: Density error decreases
cards.text: Historical check without intermediate output. The movie uses a new output-clipped run; its measurements are saved separately.

cards.title: Other checks
items: Uniform moving state preserved exactly
Mean density conserved within 10⁻⁶
64³ error below the configured threshold

cards.title: No distinct CT branch
cards.text: This validates the dedicated isothermal hydro solver. A magnetized wave would be a separate physics test with GLM and CT implementations.

cards.title: A useful future extension
cards.text: The entropy-wave page now adds an exact smooth magnetized test. Alfvén and magnetosonic propagation remain future tests.

cards.title: Watch the acoustic wave
cards.caption: 21 times · t = 0 → 0.2 · linked playback
cards.text: A new run with saved output times. The analytical wave is a linear approximation; the solver evolves nonlinear hydrodynamics.

cards.title: A wave traveling at the sound speed
cards.text: The comparison uses the small-amplitude linear acoustic solution. The simulation evolves nonlinear equations, so finite-amplitude corrections remain; this is not an exact nonlinear reference.

cards.title: What this establishes
cards.text: The smooth-wave density error decreases substantially on refinement. Two resolutions and a finite-amplitude reference do not establish a universal convergence order for shocked flows.

title: Magnetized entropy advection
description: A smooth density pattern crosses a magnetized periodic box. An exact solution lets us measure numerical error without relying on another solver.

cards.title: An exact nonlinear solution
cards.text: Uniform velocity (0.5, 0.5), pressure 1 and magnetic field (0.3, 0.2) stay constant. Density translates. Exact cell averages multiply the sinusoidal amplitude by sinc(1/N)²; initial states use the same averages.

cards.title: What this tests
cards.text: Smooth multidimensional entropy transport at finite amplitude. The uniform magnetic field does not exercise Alfvén waves, reconnection or shock capture. These still need separate tests.
